ai.description: *Cnemaspis adii* is a small gecko reaching 35 mm SVL. It features a brownish-grey body with a distinct yellow vertebral stripe and a white-spotted throat. A prominent dark post-ocular streak is present.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cnemaspis adii* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, bright yellow or orange patch on the throat, which is absent in most other similar Indian congeners.
ai.habitat: *Cnemaspis adii* inhabits moist deciduous forests in the Western Ghats, typically found on granite boulders and rock faces at elevations between 600 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: Cnemaspis adii is a diurnal gecko that actively forages for small insects on rocky surfaces during the day, utilizing its agility to navigate complex terrain.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis adii* is oviparous, laying a single, hard-shelled egg per clutch. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cnemaspis adii* is endemic to the Western Ghats of Karnataka, India, where it inhabits rocky outcrops within moist deciduous forests at elevations around 700–800 meters.
